subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天的主线，是 AI 正从“帮你完成一个任务”走向“组织一整套工作”。Agent swarm、能读写企业文件的连接器、可以连续工作数小时的新模型，都在把生产力的瓶颈从模型能力推向协作方式和边界管理。与此同时，真正重要的判断没有消失：工具要帮助人把愿景做出来，人与人的协作也不能被一群彼此隔离的 agent 取代。

archive.title: Agent 协作日报
archive.desc: AI 的下一步不只是更强的模型，而是让 agent 组成团队、进入真实文件和工作流，同时保留人的判断与协作。

sections.title: From Agents to Swarms / 从 Agent 到 Agent Swarm
sections.desc: 当 agent 不再只是单个助手，而是围绕目标自行分工，工作方式会出现新的分水岭。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie sees the next productivity jump coming from agent swarms: groups of agents that pursue a goal and find their own route to completion. The progression is clear—chat sped up interactions, single agents compressed hours into minutes, and swarms could remove the interaction bottleneck altogether.

That makes the opportunity less about building another chat interface and more about the harnesses, applied products, and FDE work that wire this pattern into coding, games, trading, science, security, and other digital environments.
original:
Agent swarms have the potential to drive yet another leap in output from AI. The impact will be a clear separation between teams that adopt this pattern of work and those that don’t.

The progression has roughly been: chat gave us quick turn AI responses that let us work a bit faster, but we were still rate limited by our interactions; then agents that can go off and complete entire tasks for us, accelerating hours or days of work into minutes; to now swarms of agents that are goal seeking and will find any route to the successful completion of a project, where there’s no inherent limit to the productivity gains.

We can imagine a future where, for any task in which value can be created within a self-contained digital environment, swarms will be able to complete the work faster than any other approach.

Essentially any area where value creation is currently bound by the amount of research you can do, the amount of decisions made with a set of software tools, the amount of data processed or consumed, and the amount of code (or code adjacent) that can be generated.

This means swarms will play a big role in game development, coding, trading, life sciences research, IT automation, cyber, math breakthroughs, animation, and plenty of other areas of work that have these characteristics.

There’s a lot of opportunity to build the harnesses, applied AI products, and infrastructure for how these agents operate. And most importantly there’s a ton of opportunity for those that can wire up work in this way. It’s going to be an entire new field of FDE work available.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 认为，下一轮生产力跃升来自 agent swarm：一群围绕目标行动、自己寻找完成路径的 agent。演进路线很清楚：chat 加快了交互，单个 agent 把几小时压缩成几分钟，而 swarm 可能彻底移除人与工具交互这一瓶颈。
所以机会不只是再做一个聊天界面，而是构建 harness、应用型产品和 FDE 工作，把这种协作模式接入编程、游戏、交易、科研、安全等数字环境。
original:
Agent swarm 有潜力再次推动 AI 的产出跃升。影响会很明确：采用这种工作模式的团队，将和不采用的团队拉开差距。

大致的演进是：chat 提供快速的 AI 响应，让工作稍微变快，但我们仍受交互次数限制；然后是能够自行完成整项任务的 agent，把几小时或几天的工作加速到几分钟；现在则是围绕目标行动的 swarm，它们会找到任何完成项目的路径，生产力收益没有内在上限。

在任何能于自包含数字环境中创造价值的任务里，swarm 都可能比其他方式更快完成工作。

这包括游戏开发、编程、交易、生命科学研究、IT 自动化、网络安全、数学突破、动画等领域。构建 agent 运作所需的 harness、应用型 AI 产品和基础设施，会带来大量机会，也会催生一整类新的 FDE 工作。

rewrite: Levie's more concrete prediction is that agents will work with enterprise files 100 times more than people do today. Box's Anthropic partnership turns that prediction into a workflow: Claude can read, edit, and write back contracts, presentations, strategy documents, and other content through MCP.

The important shift is from retrieval to authorship. Enterprise data stops being a place an agent looks things up and becomes a shared workspace where agents and people continuously produce artifacts.
original:
Agents are going to work with enterprise files 100X more than people do today. This is why we're excited to partner with Anthropic to bring full read/write interoperability to Box content via Claude.

Now you can have an agent not only pull up content to work with in a workflow, but also write back file updates to Box and view them directly inside of Claude, all via MCP. You can create, edit, and update contracts, presentations, strategy docs, and any other content.

When we started Box we couldn't have imagined all the ways that we'd be working with our unstructured data in the future, but it's clear that agents and people will be producing vastly more artifacts than we imagined. We're building the platform that makes it incredibly seamless and secure to work with your content from any agent.

rewrite: Levie 更具体的判断是：未来 agent 处理企业文件的次数会达到今天人类的 100 倍。Box 和 Anthropic 的合作把这个判断变成了工作流：Claude 可以通过 MCP 读取、编辑并写回合同、演示文稿、战略文档等内容。
关键变化是从“检索”走向“创作”。企业数据不再只是 agent 查东西的地方，而会变成 agent 和人持续共同生产内容的工作空间。
original:
Agent 处理企业文件的次数会达到今天人类的 100 倍。Box 与 Anthropic 合作，让 Claude 通过 MCP 对 Box 内容实现完整的读写互操作。

现在 agent 不仅能在工作流中调取内容，也能把更新写回 Box，并直接在 Claude 里查看。它可以创建、编辑和更新合同、演示文稿、战略文档等内容。未来 agent 和人会生产出远超想象数量的内容，Box 正在构建让任何 agent 无缝、安全地处理这些内容的平台。

sections.title: Tools That Meet the Real World / 工具进入真实工作流
sections.desc: 真正有用的 AI 产品不是一次性 demo，而是能持续协作、处理边界情况并进入已有工作环境的工具。

rewrite: Dan Shipper's day-zero test of Gemini 4 Carbon is a useful reminder that model choice is task-specific. It was substantially better at coding than Argon, could work for hours on ambitious builds, and was strong on audio, video, and 3D tasks—but it sometimes kept going past the brief and produced huge, less-modular files.
His practical rule is simple: give Carbon one large job with a clear finish line, then review the result. It is a promising second opinion, not a reason to replace every tool in the stack.
original:
BREAKING:

@Google just dropped Gemini 4 Carbon. It’s a much better coder than Argon—but I’m probably keeping Argon for writing.

We’ve been testing it at @every across coding, writing, design, and knowledge work. It can work for hours on an ambitious project, but it doesn’t always know when to stop.

Here’s your day-zero vibe check:

• Coding: On one run of our Senior Engineer benchmark, Carbon scored 44%, versus Argon’s 21%. A big improvement, though still middle of the pack. In a separate test, @hammer_mt gave it a backlog to work through. It identified 6 tasks as ready, then did 15—including work someone else was already doing. He stopped it after almost 4.5 hours.

• Big builds: @RandyCounsman gave it 3D scans of our podcast studio and an equipment list. In one attempt, it built a browser-based model accurate enough to check whether new gear would fit without getting into the shot. He estimates Carbon also wrote about 95% of a big update to Everycut, our internal video editor.

• Code quality: @kieranklaassen values its tests and documentation on large projects, including its record of approaches it considered and rejected. Fable remains his first choice, but Carbon has earned a place alongside it. The catch: It can produce huge files where Fable keeps things more modular.

• Audio and video: Randy found it caught audio editing issues other models missed. Kieran handed it a recorded meeting and asked for shorts. It came back with 6 titled clips.

• Design: @jackcheng got a hyperrealistic ginkgo-leaf app icon with details other models struggle with. Objects and 3D scenes look better than Argon’s. Interfaces split the team: Jack and Randy kept getting boxes within boxes, while @TylerNishida liked its ideas for new interfaces. Kieran says giving it design guidance makes a big difference.

• Writing: Our editorial benchmark put Carbon and Argon about even. If you like Argon, you’ll probably like Carbon. But Carbon costs more, and I haven’t seen enough improvement to justify switching.

My Reach Test: 🟨 I’ll use it sometimes.

Give it one big job with a clear finish line, and review what comes back. It’s also worth trying as a second opinion, especially on audio and video.

Full vibe check coming soon: https://t.co/Ch2pNl9Po5

rewrite: Dan Shipper 对 Gemini 4 Carbon 的 day-zero 测试提醒我们：模型选择越来越取决于任务。它的 coding 明显强于 Argon，可以连续数小时做大型项目，在音频、视频和 3D 任务上也有优势，但有时不知道该停，还会产出巨大而不够模块化的文件。
他的实用建议是：给 Carbon 一个边界清晰的大任务，然后认真审查结果。它适合作为强力的第二意见，还不是替换整套工具链的理由。
original:
Google 刚发布 Gemini 4 Carbon。它的 coding 比 Argon 好很多，但写作我可能还是用 Argon。我们在 coding、写作、设计和知识工作中测试了它。它可以连续数小时做一个有野心的项目，但不总知道什么时候该停。

在一次 Senior Engineer benchmark 中，Carbon 得分 44%，Argon 为 21%。它还完成了 3D 工作室模型、Everycut 视频编辑器更新的大约 95%，能发现其他模型漏掉的音频问题，也能从会议录音生成 6 个带标题的短片。缺点是有时会把 6 个任务做成 15 个，甚至重复别人正在做的工作；它的文件也可能很大、不够模块化。

我的结论是：偶尔会用。给它一个有明确终点的大任务，然后检查结果；特别值得在音频和视频任务上作为第二意见试试。

rewrite: Claude's new interactive connectors move integrations beyond passing data into a prompt. Users can open the full version of Adobe, Atlassian, or Box beside the conversation, make changes themselves, or ask Claude to make them together.
That is a small but important interface decision: the agent does not have to replace the tools people already use. It can become a collaborator inside the existing workspace.
original:
Also new: with interactive connectors, you can now open the full version of a tool inside Claude. Work in Adobe, Atlassian, and Box beside your conversation. Make changes yourself, or ask Claude to make them with you.

Rolling out on web and desktop. https://t.co/m2x0tcHlLn

rewrite: Claude 的 interactive connectors 让集成不再只是把数据塞进 prompt。用户可以在对话旁打开 Adobe、Atlassian 或 Box 的完整工具，自己修改，也可以让 Claude 和自己一起完成修改。
这是一个小但重要的界面选择：agent 不必替代人们已经在用的工具，而是可以直接成为现有工作空间里的协作者。
original: 新功能：通过 interactive connectors，现在可以在 Claude 里打开工具的完整版本。在对话旁使用 Adobe、Atlassian 和 Box，可以自己修改，也可以让 Claude 和你一起修改。该功能正在 Web 和桌面端推出。

sections.title: The Shape of AI-Native Software / AI 原生软件的形状
sections.desc: 当 agent 成为软件的主要使用者和协作者，产品设计与底层语言都会开始重新分化。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch argues that agentic coding will make programming languages more specialized, not less. Rust already shows what a strong ecosystem can look like; the next generation may include purpose-built languages, discretionary C, LLVM IR, or even assembly for particular use cases.
The underlying idea is that AI makes software more fluid. There is less reason to force every problem into one general-purpose language when an agent can work across a tailored stack.
original:
Rust is a superb language and ecosystem, especially given it was invented pre agentic coding.

With agents, new languages will blossom, even purpose-built ones for specific usecases, and discretionary C or even LLVM IR, assembly…

AI is fluid. No more one-size-fits-all. https://t.co/YTwRelXWCW

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 认为，agentic coding 会让编程语言变得更专用，而不是更统一。Rust 已经展示了强大语言生态的样子；下一代工具可能会包括为特定场景打造的语言，甚至直接使用 C、LLVM IR 或 assembly。
底层逻辑是：AI 让软件变得更流动。当 agent 能够跨越定制化技术栈工作，就没必要再把所有问题硬塞进一种通用语言。
original:
Rust 是非常出色的语言和生态，尤其考虑到它诞生在 agentic coding 之前。

有了 agent，新语言会大量出现，甚至是为特定用途打造的语言，也可能直接使用 C、LLVM IR 或 assembly。

AI 是流动的，不再是一种方案适合所有场景。

rewrite: Rauch's Vercel Security Review numbers make the case for agents in a less glamorous but more valuable way: in under a week, the system identified 57,897 vulnerabilities, including 6,029 critical or high severity, and an agent had already patched 14,665.
The striking part is not just the volume. It is how much security work remains invisible until an agent can continuously inspect and fix repositories, regardless of where they are deployed.
original: Vercel Security Review, less than 1 week since launch: ✓ 𝟱𝟳,𝟴𝟵𝟳 vulnerabilities identified ✓ 𝟲,𝟬𝟮𝟵 critical or high ✓ 𝟭𝟰,𝟲𝟲𝟱 already patched by Agent I'm shocked at ① the number of critical vulnerabilities that would go unnoticed and ② the ease at which the agent automatically fixes them. You can turn it on for any repo, no matter where you deploy to.

rewrite: Rauch 分享的 Vercel Security Review 数据，展示了 agent 更朴素但更有价值的一面：上线不到一周，系统发现了 57,897 个漏洞，其中 6,029 个是 critical 或 high，agent 已经修复了 14,665 个。
真正惊人的不只是数量，而是有多少安全问题原本会一直隐藏，直到 agent 能持续检查并修复仓库，而且不受部署位置限制。
original: Vercel Security Review 上线不到一周：发现 57,897 个漏洞，其中 6,029 个为 critical 或 high，agent 已经修复 14,665 个。我震惊于两件事：原本会被忽略的严重漏洞数量，以及 agent 自动修复它们的轻松程度。任何仓库都可以开启，不管部署在哪里。

sections.title: Human Collaboration Still Matters / 人的协作仍然重要
sections.desc: AI 让个人能力扩张，但更强的工具不等于更好的孤岛；产品和工作方式仍然要把人连接起来。

rewrite: Thariq Shihipar makes a useful correction to the current AI demo culture: we need fewer one-shot showcases and more tools that let people collaborate with models to bring a vision to life.
The distinction matters. A demo proves that a model can produce something once; a product has to help a person steer, revise, and keep going until the result is actually theirs.
original: we need fewer one shot demos and more tools that show how you can collaborate with models to bring your vision to life https://t.co/OlEhSqu9Mo

rewrite: Thariq Shihipar 给当下的 AI demo 文化做了一个重要纠偏：我们需要少一点一次性展示，多一点能让人和模型协作、把愿景真正做出来的工具。
区别在这里：demo 只能证明模型某一次能产出东西；产品则必须帮助人持续引导、修改和推进，直到结果真正属于自己。
original: 我们需要更少的一次性 demo，更多展示如何与模型协作、把你的愿景变成现实的工具。

rewrite: Ryo Lu pushes back on the natural endpoint of agent enthusiasm: everyone running a private army of agents in isolation. His claim is simple—'working together with other humans is where the magic happens.'

As agent capacity grows, the scarce resource may become shared context, taste, and trust between people. The best systems will amplify collaboration instead of turning every contributor into a separate automated island.
original:
working together with other humans is where the magic happens, not each of us running our own army of agents in silos

glad to see this come alive 💛 https://t.co/rGFJITKBNH

rewrite: Ryo Lu 反对 agent 热潮可能走向的一个自然终点：每个人都在孤岛里运行自己的 agent 大军。他的判断很简单：「真正的魔法发生在人与人的共同工作里。」
当 agent 的能力越来越强，稀缺资源可能变成团队之间共享的上下文、品味和信任。好的系统应该放大协作，而不是把每个人变成彼此隔离的自动化孤岛。
original: 真正的魔法发生在人与人的共同工作里，而不是我们每个人都在孤岛中运行自己的 agent 大军。很高兴看到这一点成为现实。

rewrite: Zara Zhang's advice for building an audience is deliberately unglamorous: share work in progress instead of waiting for perfection. The feedback is not just promotion; it can tell you whether a project is worth finishing at all.
That is especially relevant when AI makes it cheap to produce more. Publishing the unfinished direction becomes a way to spend human attention on the ideas that deserve another round.
original:
Step 1 of sharing your work/building an audience:

Don't wait until it's done or perfect. Share a work in progress. Sometimes that's how you figure out if it's even worth finishing.

rewrite: Zara Zhang 关于建立受众的建议朴素得有点反潮流：别等到完美才分享，先把进行中的作品拿出来。反馈不只是推广，它还能帮你判断这个项目到底值不值得做完。
当 AI 让产出变得便宜时，这一点尤其重要。尽早公开未完成的方向，能把人的注意力留给真正值得继续投入的想法。
original: 分享作品、建立受众的第一步：不要等到完成或完美，先分享进行中的作品。有时你正是通过这个过程，才知道它是否值得完成。
